statement.p: Compute the flux of \vec F=x\vec i+y\vec j+z\vec k through the curved surface of the cylinder x^2+y^2=25 bounded below by the plane x+y+z=2, above by the plane x+y+z=7, and oriented away from the z-axis.

static.solution:
\vec r=x\vec i+y\vec j+z\vec k =5\cos t\vec i+ 5\sin t\vec j + s \vec k, where 0\leq t\leq 2\pi and 2-5 \cos t-5 \sin t\leq s\leq 7 - 5 \cos t - 5\sin t.
The vector \partial \vec r/\partial t\times\partial\vec r/\partial s points away from the z-axis, so d\vec A=\left({\partial\vec r}/{\partial t}\times {\partial\vec r}/{\partial s}\right)\,ds\, dt and \vec F\cdot d\vec A = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x \amp y \amp z\\ -5\sin t \amp 5\cos t \amp 0\\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1\end{array}\right| \,ds\,dt = (5 x\cos t + 5 y\sin t)\,ds\,dt. Plugging in for x and y, this is \vec F\cdot d\vec A = 25 (\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t)\,ds\,dt = 25\, ds\,dt. Hence, \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_{2-5\cos t-5\sin t}^{7-5\cos t-5\sin t} 25\,ds\, dt = \int_0^{2\pi} 125\,dt = 250\pi.
